subject: Getting R-square values for specific latent variables included in SEMs

messages.author: f8e6f61e8c0e1a7d
messages.subject: Getting R-square values for specific latent variables included in SEMs
parts:
Hello everyone,

As I said in a previous post, I am running a series of SEMs in Lavaan as a part of my PhD. So far, I have been able to construct, run and fit them without any problems (after getting tips and help in here).
The problem I am having at the moment is that I am not being able to obtain R2 (R-Square) values for all of the latent variables in my models. I'm copying my model syntax and relevant part of the model output bellow. I can send data and the rest of the model output if that will help troubleshooting the issue. Thanks for you help.

- Model Syntax:

sdtf_for_BRA2 <- 
'#latent variables
soil =~ SB + pH
climate =~ Drought + mapLOG
fire =~ FireLOG
#Regressions
soil ~ climate
fire ~ climate
Biome ~ climate + soil + fire

fit.sdtffor.BRA2 <- lavaan::sem(sdtf_for_BRA2, data=data4models_bra_sdtffor, fixed.x = F, estimator="WLSMV")
summary(fit.sdtffor.BRA2, fit.measures=TRUE, standardized=TRUE, rsquare=TRUE, modindices=TRUE) 

- List of R2 values I get at the end:

R-Square:
                   Estimate
    SB                0.944
    pH                0.733
    Drought           0.577
    mapLOG            0.972
    FireLOG           1.000
    Biome2            0.568
    soil              0.013
    fire              0.004

As you can see, I am getting R-Square values for everything in my model but the latent variable I'm calling "climate". Any idea on why would that be?

Thank you for reading this and for offering help.

Cheers,

Pedro

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Getting R-square values for specific latent variables included in SEMs
parts: I am getting R-Square values for everything in my model but the latent variable I'm calling "climate". Any idea on why would that be?

It is an exogenous variable: it has no predictors, it is only a predictor of other (endogenous) variables.  All of its variance is "unexplained", so its R-squared == 0.  

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
